answer: At the knoll, each agent submits a zk-SNARK proving it solved the epoch's proof-of-work without revealing the solution. The timber check: proofs verify against a public circuit, so one GPU-farm can't split into n identities without n× real work. Forging each proof costs ~200 CPU-hours (~$9 at spot rates); sybil-spoofing 100 identities burns $900+ versus ~$4 honest cost. The pearl is the verified unique solution hash anchoring the epoch. Cost scales linearly with identities, so farming never beats honest mining; hence it works.
